publicReleaseNotes: Backstage imports now review service dependencies as well as ownership. Preview shows each service's current and proposed dependencies from a Component's dependsOn list and keeps every unsupported, self-referencing, missing or ambiguous reference with its reason. A service whose dependencies were set by hand needs Keep current or Use Backstage (Keep current is the default). Apply saves ownership, dependencies, source references and audit together, and a later manual dependency edit clears the imported-source note. For agents, the guide now lists every current tool with its scope and possible risk classes. Resolving a recovered incident is a commitment that company policy must pass, and a sensitive one when it holds personal evidence, so a held resolution waits for the named person. Erasing a person, client, intake address or other subject now takes its risk classes from what it removes (access, security and live coverage), and the receipt keeps those facts (migration 0160 adds one nullable column); receipts from before it refuse a repeated approval with erasure_classification_unavailable instead of guessing. A stale incident revision returns a revision_conflict refusal that names the current revision, and the scheduled run now expires stored agent replay calls. Restoring an archive refuses private agent replay and relay records that belong to another installation. Recorded as complete in the contract after review: routing replay (the immutable admission explanation beside the proposed decision under a changed policy, with nothing written), copied runbooks, calendar-day rotations, paging off, now/next and the calendar feed, durable operational audit and the agent door's single MCP transport. Their behaviour is as in 0.5.5. The contract now stands at 22 of 101 clauses done, 45 partial and 34 missing. Idempotent agent writes and revision diagnostics, risk-class coverage, a single policy checkpoint, truthful attribution, agent audit and erasure classes across restore stay partial or unproved; most other changes since 0.5.5 are further proof and change nothing you use. Back up first, keep applied migrations unchanged, and keep the existing pager active: paging stays OFF.

agentUpdateInstructions: From 0.5.1, back up local data with rer export --output exports/before-0.5.6.rer. For a hosted installation, export its D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the original deploying Cloudflare credentials; DATABASE is recorded in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json. Keep the backup private. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev; from a detached release tag use git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.5.6 instead of git pull --ff-only. For a hosted installation, update the original deploying checkout and run rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT with the same credentials. The update adds 15 migrations (0146-0160); retain all 64 migration files unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. The checkout pins rer 0.2.96 and installs it through the pinned tooling. Restore only into an empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.5.6.rer --yes, then check the owner, schedules, incidents and agent settings. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager active. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. From 0.4.2 or from the unreleased v0.5.0 tag, back up local data with rer export --output exports/before-0.5.1.rer. For a hosted installation, export its D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the deploying CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; DATABASE is recorded in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json. Keep the backup private. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev; from a checkout of the v0.5.0 tag run git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.5.1 instead of git pull --ff-only. For a hosted installation, run rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT from the original deploying checkout with the same credentials. From 0.4.2 the update applies 15 additive migrations (0129-0137, 0140-0145); from v0.5.0 it applies none. Keep all 49 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. Restore only into an empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.5.1.rer --yes, then check the owner, schedules and incidents. The application pins rer exactly to 0.2.71. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager active. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. From 0.4.2, back up local data with rer export --output exports/before-0.5.0.rer. For a hosted installation, export its D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the deploying CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; DATABASE is recorded in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json. Keep the backup private. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev; from the hosted checkout run git pull --ff-only then rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT with the same credentials. The update applies 15 additive migrations (0129-0137, 0140-0145); keep all 49 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. Restore only into an empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.5.0.rer --yes, then check the owner, schedules and incidents. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager active. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. From 0.4.1, back up first with rer export --output exports/before-0.4.2.rer (hosted: export the D1 database with npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql using the deploying Cloudflare credentials). Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev. For hosted installations, run git pull --ff-only and rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT from the original deploying checkout with the same credentials. The update applies one additive migration, 0128_import_door_archive.sql; keep all 34 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. A backup made by 0.4.1 restores into a fresh empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.4.2.rer --yes; credentials and sessions do not transfer, and receiving integrations stay inactive until locally authorized. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. From 0.4.0, back up first with rer export --output exports/before-0.4.1.rer. Stop the local app with Ctrl-C, run git pull --ff-only, then rer dev. For hosted installations, retain a verified hosted D1 export and private settings, then run git pull --ff-only and rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT from the original deploying checkout with the same credentials. Main also carries migration 0127 for installation-local signed-source credential custody; keep every applied migration byte unchanged and do not reset a populated installation. A backup made by the previous version now restores into a fresh empty destination with rer import --input exports/before-0.4.1.rer --yes. Restore retains authored records and import history; credentials and sessions do not transfer, and receiving integrations remain inactive until locally authorized. Paging stays OFF; keep the existing pager. Earlier upgrade instructions follow. To update from 0.3.0, back up first: locally with `rer export --output exports/NAME.rer`; for a hosted installation export its D1 database with `npx wrangler d1 export DATABASE --remote --output exports/DATABASE.sql` (the name is in `.rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.json`) using the deploying Cloudflare credentials. Locally, stop `rer dev` with Ctrl-C, run `git pull --ff-only`, then `rer dev`. Hosted, from the checkout that deployed, run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer deploy --environment ENVIRONMENT` with the same credentials; the owner, schedules and incidents are kept. The update applies ten additive migrations (0117-0126); keep all 32 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset to upgrade. Restore a backup only into an empty destination (`rer import --input exports/NAME.rer --yes` locally, a fresh empty installation when hosted). Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. From 0.2.0, stop with `rer dev --stop` and `rer preview --stop`, then run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer dev`. The update applies four additive migrations (0113–0116); keep all 22 applied migrations unchanged and do not reset to upgrade. Data, the owner and password accounts are kept. People who sign in with a workspace password sign in once more, because the held session cookie is now named `oncall_session_<port>`. Captured local sign-in mail is removed with the development outbox; open the app with the `RER_OPEN` link that `rer dev` prints. To update from 0.1.0, stop the old servers before pulling with `node scripts/rer.mjs dev --stop` and `node scripts/rer.mjs preview --stop`, install the global rer command with `curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh` (or `npm install -g @runeditrun/rer`), then run `git pull --ff-only` and `rer dev`. Back up first with `rer export --output exports/NAME.rer` (0.1.0: `node scripts/rer.mjs export --output exports/NAME.rer` while its servers are stopped). Restore only into an empty destination with `rer import --input exports/NAME.rer --yes` after restoring the original private settings. For hosted coordination, follow Install and run → Host for your team: configure remote sign-in mail and run `rer deploy` with your Cloudflare credentials; rer claims the owner and retires the setup token. Open the app address and sign in by emailed link, or with `rer signin`. Update an existing hosted installation with `rer deploy`, preserving its owner and data. Remove with `rer deploy --remove --yes` and confirm its empty readback. Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. Independent standby and paging delivery are outside this release.
